checklist_item.title: Verify Pre-Condition: Does tx.gasLimit > 16777216 trigger rejection path?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus-layer (beacon chain) client. Txpool gas cap enforcement is an execution-layer concern. Prysm delegates all per-transaction validation to the execution engine via Engine API (engine_newPayloadVX). The value 16777216 appears only in encoding/bytesutil/integers_test.go as a byte-encoding serialization test value, unrelated to gas caps.

phase1.summary: Prysm does not implement a transaction pool. The 16777216 gas cap constant exists in target_workspace only in bytesutil integer encoding tests (encoding/bytesutil/integers_test.go:40), completely unrelated to txpool enforcement. No txpool gas cap state machine exists in the codebase. Prysm's execution layer interface is limited to Engine API JSON-RPC calls (engine_newPayloadV1-V4).
phase1.cache_analysis: No txpool cache exists in Prysm. Not applicable.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: No per-transaction gas cap enforcement thread or goroutine exists. Not applicable.

phase2.summary: No code path exists for this check. Prysm forwards execution payloads (entire blocks) to the execution engine without inspecting individual transaction gas limits. The symbolic execution space for this property is empty.

phase2_5.summary: The txpool rejection path for oversized transactions does not exist in Prysm. All execution payload processing goes through beacon-chain/execution/engine_client.go:NewPayload which delegates to the execution engine without per-transaction gas inspection.
phase2_5.attack_surface: None - code does not exist in this target

phase3.summary: The invariant cannot be proven or disproven because the enforcement mechanism is absent from the codebase. Prysm trusts the execution engine to enforce per-transaction gas limits via the Engine API protocol.
phase3.guard_identified: None in Prysm for per-transaction gas cap
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Not applicable - enforcement is fully delegated to execution engine

phase3_5.reason: Txpool gas cap enforcement is an execution layer concern. Prysm is a consensus client and does not implement txpool logic. The 16777216 constant found in encoding/bytesutil/integers_test.go is a byte-encoding test value unrelated to gas caps. The target codebase is architecturally wrong for this check.
phase3_5.recommendation: Redirect audit to execution layer client (go-ethereum or Arbitrum Nitro) for txpool gas cap checks.

checklist_item.title: Verify Pre-Condition: Does tx.gasLimit <= 16777216 trigger acceptance path?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm is a consensus-layer client. Transaction acceptance at or below the 16777216 gas cap is an execution layer concern. Prysm accepts execution payloads wholesale based on the execution engine's validation result via engine_newPayloadVX. No per-transaction inspection occurs.

phase1.summary: Same architectural finding as CHK-0020#2. Transaction acceptance at or below the 16777216 gas cap is an execution layer concern. No acceptance path code exists in Prysm for per-transaction gas limits. Prysm's payload processing (beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go:ProcessPayload) validates parent hash, RANDAO, timestamp, and blob KZG commitment count only.

phase2.summary: No code to execute. The acceptance path for tx.gasLimit <= 16777216 is not implemented in Prysm. Prysm accepts execution payloads wholesale based on the execution engine's validation result.

phase2_5.summary: No entry point in Prysm leads to per-transaction gas acceptance logic.

phase3.summary: Invariant not implemented in Prysm. Not provable in this codebase.

phase3_5.reason: Per-transaction gas limit acceptance is an execution layer concern implemented in the execution client, not in Prysm.
phase3_5.recommendation: Redirect to execution layer client audit.

checklist_item.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does block validation catch txpool-bypassing oversized transactions?

code_scope.resolution_error: Original not_found from phase 02c; manually resolved to nearest architectural boundary

audit_items.state_context: Prysm's block validation does NOT catch oversized transactions. The trust boundary is mediated entirely by the Engine API: engine_newPayloadVX. If the execution engine accepts a payload containing oversized transactions (e.g., builder-constructed block bypassing txpool), Prysm will accept the block without independent gas re-validation. This is by design in Ethereum's consensus/execution split architecture.

phase1.summary: Prysm's block validation (ProcessPayload in beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go) checks parent hash, RANDAO, timestamp, and blob commitment count. It does not iterate transactions. Trust boundary enforcement for per-transaction gas is entirely delegated to the execution engine via engine_newPayloadVX. A transaction bypassing txpool gas cap could reach block validation if the execution engine includes it in a payload, but Prysm would not catch it.
state_anomalies_found: Prysm does not provide independent per-transaction gas validation as a defense-in-depth layer; it trusts execution engine results absolutely
phase1.cache_analysis: beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go:ProcessPayload calls st.SetLatestExecutionPayloadHeader(payload) which caches block-level GasLimit and GasUsed but does not inspect individual transactions.
phase1.concurrency_analysis: Not applicable to this specific check.

phase2.summary: An attacker constructing a block with oversized transactions could submit it via P2P. Prysm would forward the execution payload to the execution engine via engine_newPayloadVX. If the execution engine validates it as VALID, Prysm would accept the block with no independent gas check. This is a design decision, not a bug in Prysm.
phase2.counterexample: A counterexample would require the execution engine to be compromised or buggy. This is out of scope for Prysm.
attack_scenarios: Execution engine returns VALID for payload containing oversized transaction; Prysm accepts without per-transaction re-validation - but this requires execution engine compromise

phase2_5.summary: The trust boundary check is mediated by the Engine API. Prysm trusts the execution engine's response. An attacker would need to compromise the execution engine to exploit this architectural decision.
phase2_5.attack_surface: Execution engine compromise, which is outside Prysm's bug bounty scope

phase3.summary: The invariant 'Prysm independently validates per-transaction gas at block validation' does not hold and was never intended to hold. The architectural design delegates this entirely to the execution engine. No guard in Prysm provides this property.
phase3.guard_sufficiency: The guard is entirely dependent on execution engine correctness. Prysm adds no independent verification of per-transaction gas limits.
edge_cases: MEV-Boost builder-constructed blocks bypass txpool; execution engine validate_payload should still apply at EL level, but this is an execution client concern not Prysm's

phase3_5.reason: Prysm intentionally delegates per-transaction validation to the execution engine by design of the Engine API protocol. The absence of per-transaction gas validation in Prysm is correct behavior per Ethereum architecture, not a vulnerability. Any exploit requires a compromised or buggy execution engine, which is outside Prysm's scope.
phase3_5.recommendation: Audit the execution client for independent block-level per-transaction gas re-validation as a defense-in-depth measure. MEV-Boost scenarios should be audited at the relay and execution client level.

checklist_item.title: Verify Boundary Condition: Does txpool use strict comparison (> not >=) for gas cap?

audit_items.state_context: Prysm does not implement txpool or per-transaction gas cap enforcement. The proposer_bellatrix.go:expectedGasLimit() function uses strict > comparison for block-level gas limit adjustments, not per-transaction caps. This is an unrelated property.

phase1.summary: No txpool comparison operator code exists in Prysm. The check specifically asks to audit the comparison operator (> vs >=) in txpool gas cap enforcement code. No such code exists in target_workspace/. The only gas limit comparison found in Prysm is in proposer_bellatrix.go:expectedGasLimit, which computes block-level gas limit adjustments (not per-transaction caps) using arithmetic on parentGasLimit / gasLimitAdjustmentFactor (where gasLimitAdjustmentFactor = 1024). This is unrelated to the 16777216 per-transaction gas cap.

phase2.summary: No comparison operator to audit. The check cannot be executed against this codebase. The proposer_bellatrix.go:expectedGasLimit function uses correct > operators for block-level gas limit adjustment but is a different property.

phase3.summary: Off-by-one invariant at 16777216 gas cap is not implemented in Prysm. The existing expectedGasLimit() function uses > correctly for block-level gas adjustment, confirming the comparison pattern is known and used correctly in Prysm, but for a different unrelated property.

phase3_5.reason: Off-by-one at txpool gas cap comparison is an execution layer concern. No such comparison exists in Prysm. The only gas comparison (expectedGasLimit, proposer_bellatrix.go:446-462) correctly uses > for block-level purposes but is an unrelated property.
phase3_5.recommendation: Redirect to execution layer client. Specifically examine go-ethereum's txpool.validateTx() or equivalent in Arbitrum Nitro for the strict > vs >= comparison on the 16777216 gas cap.

checklist_item.title: Verify Boundary Condition: Does block validation use identical comparison to txpool?

audit_items.state_context: This check requires cross-layer consistency between txpool comparison operator and block validation comparison operator. Neither layer exists in Prysm for per-transaction gas limits. The Ethereum consensus/execution split architecture means this consistency property inherently spans two separate codebases (execution client for both txpool and block-level per-transaction validation, vs consensus client Prysm for consensus validation).

phase1.summary: This check requires verifying consistency between txpool and block validation comparison operators for the 16777216 gas cap. Neither the txpool nor per-transaction gas cap validation exists in Prysm. Block validation in ProcessPayload (beacon-chain/core/blocks/payload.go) does not inspect individual transaction gas limits. The GasLimit field in execution payload headers is a block-level aggregate, not a per-transaction cap.
phase1.cache_analysis: GasLimit in the cached payload header (via st.SetLatestExecutionPayloadHeader) is block-level, not per-transaction. Not related to the 16777216 cap.

phase2.summary: No comparison to check for consistency. Both the txpool layer and per-transaction block validation layer are absent from Prysm. The consistency property is architecturally unverifiable in this codebase.
attack_scenarios: Inconsistency between txpool and block validation comparison operators would exist in the execution client (geth/Nitro), not in Prysm

phase2_5.summary: No entry point leads to per-transaction gas comparison in Prysm.
phase2_5.attack_surface: None in Prysm; must audit execution layer client for both layers

phase3.summary: Consistency invariant between txpool and block validation comparison operators is not implementable in Prysm since it is a single-layer (consensus only) client. The execution/consensus split architecture means this property inherently spans two codebases.
edge_cases: Post-Merge architecture requires auditing go-ethereum/Nitro source for both txpool and block validation for this consistency check; the two layers live in the same execution client codebase

phase3_5.reason: Both comparison operators being checked (txpool and block validation) are execution layer concerns absent from Prysm. The Ethereum consensus/execution split architecture means this consistency property must be audited in the execution client. Prysm is the wrong target for this check.
phase3_5.recommendation: Audit go-ethereum or Arbitrum Nitro for consistency between pool.validateTx() and state_transition per-transaction gas validation. Specifically check that both use identical threshold (> 16777216, strict) consistently to avoid off-by-one discrepancies.
